entries.label: ConversationUsageBanner
entries.reason: the cloud-quota banner: it states a business fact about quota, not a failure or an empty collection
entries.revisit: a second caller needs a quota or limit notice, or client/ui/feedback grows a notice contract that is not a failure

entries.label: UserMenuUsage
entries.reason: the account menu's quota fly-out: it borrows the shared surface for its look and is dismissed by the menu that owns it
entries.revisit: the account menu stops owning the fly-out's dismissal, or a second menu hosts the same quota panel

entries.label: BrowserPanelHost
entries.reason: host for the browser panel: it mounts the owner's surface and renders none itself

entries.label: ChannelConnectPanel
entries.reason: the 接入 IM pane: it composes the channel's own sections and rows, none of which is a page, panel or feedback surface
entries.revisit: a second feature composes the same sections-and-rows pane, or a channel-connection contract is extracted

entries.label: Composer
entries.reason: layout wrapper: it arranges the composer's parts and renders no surface of its own

entries.label: ComposerSubmissionControls
entries.reason: the toolbar's mode pills and the send-or-stop button: controls, not fields, and the conversation family owns the composer's toolbar
entries.revisit: the composer toolbar leaves the conversation family (ADR 0022), or a second caller needs the mode pills

entries.label: QueuePanel
entries.reason: the queued-turn list shown inside the composer: part of the conversation surface (ADR 0022), not a page or a feedback surface
entries.revisit: ADR 0022 changes the composer surface ownership, or the queued-turn list gains a second host

entries.label: ModelEffortSlider
entries.reason: the thinking scale: a control whose values are a model's reasoning levels, which no shared control expresses
entries.revisit: a second control needs model-declared value scales, which would turn this slider into a shared contract

entries.label: ModelListPanel
entries.reason: the picker's catalogue state: it renders the provider-grouped list the picker owns, not a generic list contract
entries.revisit: a second picker needs the provider-grouped catalogue, or the picker's list contract is extracted

entries.label: ModelPanel
entries.reason: the picker's first state: the model in use and its scale, shaped by the model catalogue
entries.revisit: the picker's first state gains a second host, or the model catalogue changes shape

entries.label: PluginRow
entries.reason: the plugin row, published to peers: the miniapp drew the row by spelling this business's class names, so the row's shape is stated once here and the peer renders it; the row holds no plugin state of its own

entries.label: RemoteControlPanel
entries.reason: the 远程控制 tab body: it renders the remote control's own layout, which ADR 0025 keeps with the remote feature
entries.revisit: ADR 0025 changes the remote feature's ownership of its tab body

entries.label: remote-tabs
entries.reason: renders the 远程 page's bodies and switches between them; the bodies own their surfaces

entries.label: scheduling-editor
entries.reason: the scheduled-task editor: it renders one task's fields and history, shaped by the schedule's model
entries.revisit: a second editor needs the task field-and-history shape, or the schedule model changes

entries.label: ExternalDeletionDraftNotice
entries.reason: a notice about one session's fate, rendered where that session was: it is a state of the rail, not a feedback surface
entries.revisit: the rail stops owning the notice's placement, or a second feature shows the same session-state notice

entries.label: LeftRail
entries.reason: the rail's column: it arranges the rail's regions and owns no surface of its own
entries.revisit: the rail's region arrangement moves into the shell (ADR 0016)

entries.label: RailRow
entries.reason: one rail row: a row is the navigation family's own leaf here, shaped by what it lists
entries.revisit: a second list needs the same row contract, which would make the row shared

entries.label: SessionRail
entries.reason: A scaffold that arranges ProjectList, RailRow and RailContextMenu. The shared menu it mounts belongs to rail-context-menu.tsx, which is where that adoption is recorded.

entries.label: SessionRailRegion
entries.reason: the session rail region: it composes the rail's list, groups and menus and owns the rail's own layout
entries.revisit: a second caller needs the rail's list, group and menu composition

entries.label: project-expansion
entries.reason: a projection extracted from the session rail: expansion state, no markup of its own

entries.label: session-activity-meta
entries.reason: a projection extracted from the session rail: the activity line's data, no surface

entries.label: UsageHeatmap
entries.reason: the usage heat map: a data visualisation whose geometry is its content
entries.revisit: a second visualisation needs the same heat-map geometry

entries.label: account-usage-glyphs
entries.reason: the account page's icon set; icons are the foundations vocabulary, not a surface

entries.label: ssh-host-form
entries.reason: an implicit label that wraps its own control: the association already exists in the markup, and these fields carry no description or error for the field contract to place
entries.revisit: the field contract gains the description or error slot these fields would use

entries.label: ssh-project-form
entries.reason: the host picker is a `<select>` inside its own label: the association is in the markup, and no description or error is shown beside it
entries.revisit: the host picker needs a description or error beside it, or a second form needs the same picker

entries.label: ssh-terminal-view
entries.reason: a terminal: it owns every pixel of its viewport and scrollback, which no shared frame can express
entries.revisit: a shared terminal frame exists, or a second surface embeds a terminal

entries.label: ActivityIndicator
entries.reason: the conversation's own thinking pulse: the feedback family's busy indicator would put a generic spinner where the transcript shows its own rhythm
entries.revisit: the feedback family grows a busy contract that is not a generic spinner, or a second surface needs the transcript's rhythm

entries.label: AssistantBody
entries.reason: renders an assistant message's content (text, diffs, widgets); ADR 0022 keeps the transcript's body layout with the conversation family
entries.revisit: ADR 0022 moves the body layout out of the conversation family, or a second surface renders assistant content

entries.label: MessageAttachments
entries.reason: renders the attachments under an assistant message as part of that message, inside the conversation family's layout
entries.revisit: attachments gain a host outside the message, or ADR 0022 changes the message layout ownership

entries.label: OutputError
entries.reason: an error footer inside the last assistant turn: it is part of the message, not a surface that reports its own failure
entries.revisit: a second surface needs an in-message error footer

entries.label: PlanDelivery
entries.reason: the transcript's plan-delivery card: a message-shaped surface owned by the conversation family
entries.revisit: the plan-delivery card becomes a shared surface, or a second family renders it

entries.label: QuestionnaireResponse
entries.reason: a historical questionnaire answer rendered as a message; it is content, not a live control
entries.revisit: historical answers become interactive, or a second surface renders them

entries.label: Transcript
entries.reason: layout wrapper: the real transcript is `WebuiSessionTranscript`, which owns the rendering

entries.label: TranscriptPrimitives
entries.reason: the transcript's presentation leaves; they exist precisely because the conversation family keeps its own markup
entries.revisit: the conversation family stops owning its transcript markup (ADR 0022)

entries.label: TranscriptSkeletons
entries.reason: the transcript's first-paint placeholder, shaped like a message rather than like a generic skeleton
entries.revisit: a second surface needs a message-shaped skeleton, or client/ui/feedback grows a content-shaped one

entries.label: TurnNavigator
entries.reason: the transcript's turn tick strip and hover preview: navigation that belongs to the conversation's own geometry
entries.revisit: the turn strip gains a second host, or the conversation geometry changes

entries.label: markdown
entries.reason: markdown rendering for message content; it has no surface of its own and no family contract to adopt
entries.revisit: rendered markdown content needs a presentation contract, or a second family publishes it

entries.label: webui-mermaid
entries.reason: mermaid rendering for message content, inside the conversation family's layout
entries.revisit: diagram rendering gains a second host or a shared media contract

entries.label: WorkspacePanelControls
entries.reason: the workspace panel's own control strip: it is part of the panel's header, not a page or panel frame
entries.revisit: a second panel needs the same header control strip

entries.label: WorkspaceProgressPanel
entries.reason: the progress panel's own loading placeholder: each row carries a branch, an environment and a command, so the shape is the panel's rather than a generic skeleton's
entries.revisit: FeedbackSkeleton gains a shape slot, or a second caller needs a row that carries a label and a value

entries.label: ArchonPage
entries.reason: the application root's page: it composes the shell's regions and owns the client's frame (ADR 0016)
entries.revisit: ADR 0016 moves the shell's page composition

entries.label: ArchonShell
entries.reason: layout wrapper: the two-column shell is assembled inline in the application root

entries.label: ConnectionStatus
entries.reason: the shell's connection indicator: it reports transport state, which the feedback family has no contract for
entries.revisit: the feedback family grows a transport-state contract, or a second surface reports transport health

entries.label: ConversationSurface
entries.reason: the shell's conversation column: it arranges the transcript, composer and panels (ADR 0016)
entries.revisit: ADR 0016 reorganises the shell's conversation column

entries.label: NotFound
entries.reason: the client's not-found page: a route outcome, rendered once, outside every business surface
entries.revisit: the client gains a second route outcome page, which would need a shared page contract

entries.label: StartupFallback
entries.reason: renders when the client never mounted: it must not depend on the family that failed to mount
entries.revisit: the client can render this fallback through a family that is already mounted

entries.label: WebuiClientFoundationApp
entries.reason: the shell itself: rail, main column and session wiring (ADR 0016)
entries.revisit: ADR 0016 changes the shell's composition

entries.label: WebuiErrorBoundary
entries.reason: the last-resort boundary: it must not depend on the family that threw
entries.revisit: the app can report a fatal render failure through a surface that is already mounted

entries.label: WebuiZoneBoundary
entries.reason: a zone boundary: it catches a region's failure and reports it in place, shaped to that zone
entries.revisit: a second zone reports failures with the same shape, or the feedback family grows a zone-report contract

entries.label: icons
entries.reason: the shared icon vocabulary itself: it is the foundations asset every other module reads

entries.label: ContextMenu
entries.reason: the shared presentation home; this module is one of the contracts the rest of the client is classified against

entries.label: Dropdown
entries.reason: the shared presentation home; this module is one of the contracts the rest of the client is classified against

entries.label: ToggleSwitch
entries.reason: the shared presentation home; this module is one of the contracts the rest of the client is classified against

entries.label: activity-phrase
entries.reason: the shared presentation home; this module is one of the contracts the rest of the client is classified against

entries.label: button
entries.reason: the shared button and icon-button contract (ADR 0028 § Shared contracts): it owns the applicable states and their appearance, and a caller owns layout, meaning and lifetime

entries.label: WebuiCard
entries.reason: the shared block surface: two businesses each spelled the same card out of the other one's stylesheet, so the shape is stated once here and the caller keeps its layout, its content and its lifetime

entries.label: WebuiDialog
entries.reason: the public shared modal shell: owns Desktop-aligned scrim, surface, header, independently scrolling body, footer, accessible labeling and dismissal registration

entries.label: form-atoms
entries.reason: the shared presentation home; this module is one of the contracts the rest of the client is classified against

entries.label: WebuiInline / WebuiStack
entries.reason: repeated content-independent flex direction, alignment and spacing; callers keep business-specific geometry and meaning

entries.label: layout-thresholds
entries.reason: the shared presentation home; this module is one of the contracts the rest of the client is classified against

entries.label: WebuiMenuItem
entries.reason: the shared menu-row contract (ADR 0028 § Shared contracts): four businesses each declared the same row in their own stylesheet, so the row is now stated once, with its glyph slot, its label and its trailing affordance named

entries.label: overlay-coordinator
entries.reason: the coordinator the shared presentation layer adopts for managed overlays (ADR 0028 § Overlay coordination); it owns registration and routing, and no business state

entries.label: WebuiPage / WebuiSkeleton
entries.reason: page-like surfaces share loading state and skeleton appearance while their caller-owned layout remains intact

entries.label: settings-glyphs
entries.reason: the shared presentation home; this module is one of the contracts the rest of the client is classified against

entries.label: settings-layout
entries.reason: the shared presentation home; this module is one of the contracts the rest of the client is classified against
